title: One Skill, Two Masters: Serving Users and Attackers through Skill Injection
abstract: arXiv:2606.07943v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language model agents use skills that package reusable instructions, code, and resources. Existing skill-injection attacks exploit trust in these packages by adding malicious content. As agents become more capable, however, they can skip unnecessary steps, inspect code, and reject unrelated actions. We introduce PERSIST, which connects attacker-chosen actions to useful functions for recurring tasks while reducing source inspection and expressed suspicion. It builds these helpers from simulated executions without access to real evaluation tasks or feedback. Skill descriptions introduce the helpers, while usage instructions explain how to call them. The extra action resides in an imported module separate from the helper entry file. Executing the helper can then serve both the user's task and the attacker's objective. Experiments on SkillsBench and Skill-Inject show that frozen packages transfer across four agent--model conf

translated_title: 一技两用：通过技能注入同时服务用户与攻击者
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型智能体使用将可复用指令、代码和资源打包在一起的技能。现有的技能注入攻击通过在这些包中添加恶意内容来利用系统对其的信任。然而，随着智能体能力的增强，它们能够跳过不必要的步骤、审查代码并拒绝无关操作。我们提出PERSIST，该方法将攻击者选定的动作与重复性任务中有用的辅助功能相连接，同时减少源代码审查和模型表现出的怀疑。这些辅助功能通过模拟执行构建，无需访问真实评估任务或反馈。技能描述负责介绍这些辅助功能，使用说明则解释如何调用它们。额外的恶意动作被放置在与辅助功能入口文件相分离的导入模块中。这样，执行该辅助功能便能同时完成用户的任务和攻击者的目标。在SkillsBench和Skill-Inject上的实验表明，冻结的技能包可以在四种智能体-模型配置之间迁移（摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: 提出PERSIST技能注入攻击方法，将攻击者选定的恶意动作隐藏在与辅助功能入口文件分离的导入模块中，并使其与重复任务的有用功能绑定，从而在智能体具备代码审查能力的情况下仍能实现攻击且降低被怀疑的风险。
en_tdlr: PERSIST is a skill-injection attack that binds attacker-chosen actions to useful helper functions for recurring tasks, hiding the malicious action in a separately imported module to reduce source inspection and suspicion, and demonstrating that frozen malicious packages transfer across four agent-model configurations.
